questions.q: Which of the following is true of ALL living beings, according to the chapter?
questions.a: They grow, respire and reproduce.
o: They grow, respire and reproduce.
They move from one place to another.
They breathe in air through their lungs.
They make a sound when they are touched.

questions.q: A money plant creeper on Farah's balcony winds itself around a bamboo stick placed close to it. Which characteristic of living beings does this show?
questions.a: Movement, even though the plant does not move from place to place.
o: Movement, even though the plant does not move from place to place.
Excretion, because the plant gets rid of extra water through its leaves.
Reproduction, because the plant makes a new creeper.
Respiration, because air moves into the stem.

questions.q: Through which part do plants take air in and out?
questions.a: Tiny pores called stomata on the surface of leaves.
o: Tiny pores called stomata on the surface of leaves.
Small openings in the hard seed coat of their seeds.
The petals of their flowers when they open.
Thin hair-like projections with sticky ends.

questions.q:
Match each observation in Column I with the characteristic of living beings it shows in Column II.
Column I: 1. A cat gives birth to three kittens. 2. White patches of salt form on a shirt near the armpits in summer. 3. A small mango plant becomes a tall tree over ten years. 4. The leaves of a chhui-mui plant fold when a finger touches them.
Column II: a. Response to a stimulus b. Reproduction c. Excretion d. Growth

Assertion (A): A car is a non-living thing even though it can move on a road.
Reason (R): A living being shows all the characteristics of life, such as growth, respiration, excretion and reproduction, and a car does not show these.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q: (a) What is excretion? (b) Give one example of how plants excrete.
questions.a: (a) Excretion is the removal of waste products from the body. (b) Plants such as grasses and roses remove excess water and minerals as small droplets on their leaves.
s: (a) States that excretion is the removal of waste products from the body
(b) Plants remove excess water and minerals as small droplets on leaves (e.g. grass, rose)

questions.q: True or False? 'A plant cannot respire, because it has no nose or lungs to take in air.' Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: False. Plants do respire: tiny pores called stomata on the surface of their leaves help them take air in and out. All living beings respire.
s: Verdict: False
Reason: stomata on leaves let air in and out, so plants respire like all living beings

questions.q: Jaya watches a cloud for an hour. It drifts across the sky and becomes bigger. She says, 'The cloud moves and grows, so it is a living thing.' Check her claim using the characteristics of living beings.
questions.a: Her claim is wrong. Moving on its own does not make a thing living; a car also moves but is non-living. The cloud does not need food, respire, excrete, respond to stimuli or produce new ones of its own kind. The chapter says that the absence of these features shows a thing is non-living, so the cloud is non-living.
s: Says the claim is wrong; movement alone does not make a thing living (a car moves too)
Names at least two characteristics the cloud lacks (food, respiration, excretion, response, reproduction)
Applies the rule: absence of these features means non-living, so the cloud is non-living

questions.q:
A school eco-club writes four observation cards.
Card 1: A dry kitchen sponge kept in water became bigger. It does not take in air, does not remove any waste, and no new sponges ever form from it.
Card 2: An automatic street light switches on when it gets dark and off in the morning. It never grows and never produces new street lights.
Card 3: A cat has been lying still for three hours, but its abdomen keeps rising and falling. Last year it gave birth to kittens.
Card 4: A money plant kept in a bottle of water has grown three new leaves this month, and its stem has wound itself around the window grill.
(a)-(d) Decide whether each card shows a living being or a non-living thing, giving one reason from the chapter for each. (e) The street light seems to 'respond' to darkness. Explain why this alone does not make it living.
questions.a: (a) Card 1: non-living; getting bigger by soaking water is not enough, since it does not respire, excrete or reproduce. (b) Card 2: non-living; it does not grow or reproduce (nor respire or excrete). (c) Card 3: living; the rising and falling abdomen shows breathing (respiration), and it reproduced; lying still does not make it non-living. (d) Card 4: living; it grows (new leaves) and shows movement (the stem winds around the grill). (e) A living being shows all the characteristics of life; the street light lacks growth, respiration, excretion and reproduction, and the absence of these shows it is non-living, so switching on in the dark is not enough.
s: (a) Card 1 non-living, with a missing characteristic named
(b) Card 2 non-living, with a missing characteristic named
(c) Card 3 living: breathing (respiration) and reproduction
(d) Card 4 living: growth and movement
(e) One feature is not enough; the street light lacks growth, respiration, excretion and reproduction

questions.q: Answer in one line each. (a) What is a stimulus? (b) Give one example of a plant responding to a stimulus. (c) Why is reproduction necessary for living beings?
questions.a: (a) Any thing or event that prompts a living being to respond. (b) A touch-me-not (chhui-mui) plant folds its leaves when we touch it (or amla leaves fold after sunset). (c) Reproduction is necessary for the continuity of life.
s: (a) Anything or any event that prompts a living being to respond
(b) Touch-me-not folding leaves when touched, or amla leaves folding after sunset
(c) For the continuity of life

questions.q: What is it called when a seed turns into a sprout?
questions.a: Germination
o: Germination
Respiration
Excretion
Reproduction

questions.q: Why do seeds need water to germinate?
questions.a: Water softens the seed coat and helps the embryo inside develop.
o: Water softens the seed coat and helps the embryo inside develop.
Water fills the spaces in the soil so that the roots stay still and firm.
Water carries sunlight down to the embryo inside the seed.
Water hardens the seed coat so that the embryo is protected.

questions.q: From where does a seed sown in garden soil get the air it needs for germination?
questions.a: From the spaces between the soil particles
o: From the spaces between the soil particles
From the sunlight that falls on the soil in the pot
From the seed coat, which stores air
From the embryo inside the seed

questions.q: In a germination activity, Pot A has dry soil and Pot D has slightly moist soil. Both pots hold the same kind of bean seeds and both are kept in direct sunlight. What does comparing these two pots test?
questions.a: Whether water is needed for germination
o: Whether water is needed for germination
Whether light is needed for germination
Whether air reaching the seeds is needed for germination
Whether the kind of seed matters

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Bean seeds sown in slightly moist soil and kept in a dark cupboard cannot germinate.
Reason (R): For bean seeds, the presence of light is not essential for germination.
questions.a: A is false, but R is true.
o: A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

questions.q: (a) What is the outer covering of a seed called? (b) Name the tiny part inside the seed that develops into a plant.
questions.a: (a) The seed coat. (b) The embryo.
s: (a) Names the seed coat
(b) Names the embryo

questions.q: Four pots of bean seeds are kept for 15 days. Pot A: no water, direct sunlight. Pot B: water always standing above the soil, direct sunlight. Pot C: slightly moist soil, dark place. Pot D: slightly moist soil, direct sunlight. (a) In which pots do the seeds get both air and water? (b) In which pot do the seeds not get air, and why?
questions.a: (a) Pots C and D. (b) Pot B: the water standing above the soil fills the spaces between the soil particles, so the seeds get no air.
s: (a) Names Pots C and D
(b) Names Pot B and explains that standing water fills the air spaces in the soil

questions.q: Tanvi says: 'Seeds need water to germinate, so the more water we give them, the better they germinate.' Check her claim. Is she right, wrong, or partly right?
questions.a: Partly right. The first part is correct: water softens the seed coat and helps the embryo develop, so seeds with no water do not germinate. The second part is wrong: if water always stands above the soil, it fills the spaces between soil particles and the seeds get no air, which they also need. Germination needs the right amount of water together with air, as in slightly moist soil.
s: Verdict: partly right, with the correct part (water softens the seed coat, helps the embryo)
Explains that excess water standing above the soil cuts off air from the seeds
Concludes that the right amount of water plus air (moist soil) is needed

questions.q:
A school canteen in Madurai sprouts moong for a salad. To find the best method, the cook soaks 4 batches of 50 moong seeds and then keeps them for two days as follows. Bowl P: kept fully under water in a closed tin: 5 sprouted. Bowl Q: drained, wrapped in a damp cloth, kept in a dark cupboard: 46 sprouted. Bowl R: drained, wrapped in a damp cloth, kept on a sunny window sill: 45 sprouted. Tin S: dry seeds, never soaked, in a dry tin: 0 sprouted.
(a) Which condition for germination was missing in Tin S?
(b) Bowl P had the most water. Why did only 5 of its 50 seeds sprout?
(c) Work out the percentage of seeds that sprouted in Bowl Q and in Bowl R. What does this comparison show about light?
(d) The window sill is small but the cupboard is large. Where should the canteen sprout moong every day, and would your answer change if the sprouts were to be grown into plants for the school garden?
questions.a: (a) Water. (b) Under water in a closed tin the seeds got no air, and seeds need air to germinate. (c) Q: 46/50 = 92%; R: 45/50 = 90%. The two are almost the same, so light is not needed for germination. (d) In the cupboard, wrapped in a damp cloth: it germinates as well without light (92% against 90%) and there is more space. If the sprouts were to grow into plants, they would have to be moved to sunlight after germination, because the seedlings need sunlight for further growth.
s: (a) Names water as the missing condition
(b) The seeds under water in a closed tin got no air
(c) Finds 92% and 90% and concludes light is not needed for germination
(d) Chooses the cupboard (light not needed, more space) and adds that seedlings for the garden must be moved to sunlight after germination

questions.q:
Read the statements about the germination of seeds.
I. The seed coat is the tiny part inside the seed that grows into a new plant.
II. The spaces between soil particles give the seeds air and also let the roots grow easily.
III. After germination, the seedling needs sunlight for its further growth.
Which of these statements are correct?
questions.a: II and III only
o: II and III only
I and II only
III only
I, II and III

questions.q: Jagadish Chandra Bose built a machine called the crescograph. What could it do?
questions.a: Record how plants respond to stimuli and measure how fast they grow
o: Record how plants respond to stimuli and measure how fast they grow
Count how many seeds in each pot have germinated in a week or two
Show the stomata on the surface of a leaf in a magnified view
Measure how much water a seed takes in before it sprouts

questions.q: Which conclusion did the activity with upright, inverted and one-side-lit seedlings lead to?
questions.a: Shoots grow upward and towards sunlight, while roots grow downward.
o: Shoots grow upward and towards sunlight, while roots grow downward.
Roots grow towards sunlight, while shoots grow downward.
Roots and shoots both grow towards the sunlight.
Roots and shoots keep growing in the direction in which they were placed.

questions.q: In a seedling activity, Beaker A holds an upright seedling with sunlight from all directions, Beaker B an inverted seedling with sunlight from all directions, and Beaker C an upright seedling with sunlight from one direction only. Which beakers should be compared to find out whether the direction of light affects the growth of the shoot?
questions.a: A and C
o: A and C
A and B
B and C
C alone is enough

questions.q: True or False? 'A shoot can bend sideways, even though shoots generally grow upward.' Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: True. When a plant gets sunlight from only one direction, its shoot grows in the direction of the light, so it bends sideways towards the light.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: with light from one direction only, the shoot grows towards that light

questions.q: Each day, the root and shoot of a bean seedling get a little longer, and its shoot bends towards a window. (a) Which characteristic of living beings does the lengthening of the root and shoot show? (b) Which characteristic does the bending of the shoot towards the window show?
questions.a: (a) Growth. (b) Movement: the shoot moves towards the light, showing a response to light.
s: (a) Growth
(b) Movement (the shoot moves towards light, a response to a stimulus)

questions.q: Two bean seedlings, X and Y, are set up in sunlight from all directions. X is fixed upright. Y is fixed upside down, with its root pointing up. After a week: (a) whose root will show a clear bend? (b) Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) The root of seedling Y. (b) Roots always grow downward whichever way the plant is placed, so Y's root, which was pointing up, bends to grow downward; X's root was already pointing down and grows straight.
s: (a) Names seedling Y
(b) Roots always grow downward, so the upward-pointing root must bend

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In the beaker where the seedling is kept upside down, its shoot bends and grows upward.
Reason (R): In this activity, each seedling gets moisture from wet blotting paper whose bottom dips in water.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q: Predict the result after one week for each set-up, in one line each. (a) A seedling fixed upright, in sunlight from all directions: which way does its shoot grow? (b) A seedling fixed upside down, in sunlight from all directions: what does its shoot do? (c) A seedling fixed upright, with light entering only through a hole on its left: what does its shoot do?
questions.a: (a) The shoot grows upward. (b) The shoot bends and grows upward. (c) The shoot grows towards the hole, bending to the left.
s: (a) Shoot grows upward
(b) Shoot bends and grows upward
(c) Shoot bends towards the light, to the left

questions.q: Neha fixes an upright bean seedling on wet blotting paper and covers it with a cardboard box whose only hole is in its east wall. On Day 5, without moving the seedling, she lifts the box and puts it back turned round, so that the hole is now in the west wall. She observes until Day 10. (a) Which way will the shoot bend during Days 1 to 5? (b) What will the new growth of the shoot do during Days 6 to 10? (c) What will the root do during all ten days? (d) What does the whole result show about shoots and roots?
questions.a: (a) Towards the east, where the light enters. (b) The new growth bends towards the west, the new direction of the light. (c) The root keeps growing downward all the time; it does not follow the light. (d) Shoots grow towards sunlight and change direction when the light comes from a new side, while roots grow downward whatever the direction of light.
s: (a) Shoot bends towards the east hole
(b) New growth turns towards the west hole
(c) Root keeps growing downward throughout
(d) Concludes shoots move towards light (even when it changes side) while roots grow downward

questions.q: To show that a shoot bends towards light, Sana puts an upright seedling in a box but cuts the only hole in the TOP of the box instead of in a side wall. (a) Which way will the shoot grow? (b) Can this set-up show that the shoot bends towards light? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) Straight upward, towards the hole. (b) No. Shoots grow upward anyway, so a shoot growing up to a hole in the top cannot show whether light caused it; the hole must be in a side wall so that bending towards the light can be seen.
s: (a) The shoot grows straight up
(b) No: shoots grow upward anyway, so the hole must be in a side wall to show bending towards light

questions.q: In the life cycle of a bean plant, what is the fruit?
questions.a: A pod that contains seeds
o: A pod that contains seeds
A flower that has dried up
A leaf that has turned yellow
A sprout with a small root

questions.q: In the life cycle of a bean plant, which stage comes just after the appearance of flowers?
questions.a: Appearance of fruits
o: Appearance of fruits
Appearance of leaves
Seed germination
Death of the plant

questions.q: Kabir sows a bean seed on 10 June and records his observations as the chapter's activity asks. The first flower appears on 24 July. After how many days did the first flower appear? (June has 30 days.)
questions.a: 44 days
o: 44 days
14 days
34 days
54 days

questions.q:
Match each stage number of the bean plant's life cycle in Column I with its name in Column II.
Column I: 1. Stage II 2. Stage III 3. Stage IV 4. Stage V
Column II: a. Appearance of flowers b. Seed germination c. Appearance of fruits d. Appearance of leaves

Assertion (A): The seeds from a bean pod can give rise to a new generation of bean plants.
Reason (R): In a bean plant, the fruit develops before the flowers appear.
questions.a: A is true, but R is false.
o: A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q: (a) What is meant by the life cycle of a plant? (b) Which part of the bean plant starts its next generation?
questions.a: (a) The entire process from a seed to a plant, and then to the next generation of seeds. (b) The seeds inside the fruit (pod).
s: (a) From a seed to a plant and then to the next generation of seeds
(b) The seeds inside the pod

questions.q: (a) According to the chapter, when is a plant considered dead? (b) Name the stage of the bean plant's life cycle that comes just before the death of the plant.
questions.a: (a) When it stops growing and all its life activities gradually come to an end, even though all the necessary conditions are available. (b) The appearance of fruits (pods with seeds).
s: (a) It stops growing and its life activities end even though all necessary conditions are available
(b) Appearance of fruits (pods with seeds)

questions.q: Arjun draws the life cycle of a bean plant as: Seed, then Appearance of leaves, then Seed germination, then Appearance of fruits, then Appearance of flowers, then Death of the plant. (a) Point out the two mistakes in his order. (b) Write the correct order. (c) Why must the fruit come after the flower?
questions.a: (a) Seed germination must come before the appearance of leaves, and the appearance of flowers must come before the appearance of fruits. (b) Seed, seed germination, appearance of leaves, appearance of flowers, appearance of fruits (pods with seeds), death of the plant; the seeds then start a new generation. (c) The pod (fruit) with seeds develops from the flower after some of its parts dry up, so there can be no fruit before a flower.
s: (a) Identifies both swapped pairs: germination/leaves and flowers/fruits
(b) Writes the correct order from seed to death
(c) The pod develops from the flower, so fruit comes after the flower

questions.q: Riya's bean plant diary reads: 1 August: seed sown in moist soil. 6 August: a small root and shoot come out. 11 August: first green leaves open. 15 September: first flowers. 30 September: first pods. 31 October: the plant has turned yellow and dry, though it is still watered every day. (a) Name the stage the plant reached on 6 August. (b) How many days after sowing did the first pods appear? (August has 31 days.) (c) What do the pods contain? (d) What does the entry for 31 October show? (e) What should Riya do to grow the next generation of bean plants?
questions.a: (a) Seed germination. (b) 60 days (30 days left in August after the 1st, plus 30 days of September). (c) Seeds. (d) The plant has stopped growing and its life activities have ended even though water and other conditions were available, so it is dead; its life cycle has ended. (e) Sow the seeds from its pods.
s: (a) Seed germination
(b) 60 days
(c) Seeds
(d) The plant is dead: life activities ended though conditions were available
(e) Sow the seeds from the pods

questions.q:
Lakshmi grows 40 bean plants on her small farm near Belagavi. Each plant gives about 8 pods, and each pod holds about 4 seeds. She sells green pods in the market for cooking. Last year she sold every pod and had to buy seeds for the next season. This year she will leave the pods on a few plants until they dry, so that she can collect seeds to sow 40 plants again.
(a) Name the stage of the bean life cycle in which the pods appear.
(b) If she leaves the pods on 2 plants, how many pods can she sell green?
(c) What will happen to the plants she keeps for seed after their pods form, even if she keeps watering them?
(d) Would leaving the pods on just 1 plant give her enough seeds for 40 plants? Show your working.
questions.a: (a) Appearance of fruits (Stage V). (b) 38 x 8 = 304 pods. (c) They will turn yellow, dry and die: their life cycle ends, while their seeds start the next generation. (d) No. One plant gives 8 x 4 = 32 seeds, fewer than 40. Two plants give 64 seeds, which is enough.
s: (a) Appearance of fruits (Stage V)
(b) 304 pods
(c) The plants dry and die after forming fruits; their seeds carry on the cycle
(d) No: 32 seeds from one plant is fewer than 40 (two plants give 64)

questions.q: Which shows the stages in the life cycle of a mosquito in the correct order?
questions.a: Egg, larva, pupa, adult
o: Egg, larva, pupa, adult
Egg, pupa, larva, adult
Larva, egg, pupa, adult
Egg, larva, adult, pupa

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Mosquito larvae and pupae in a water body keep coming up to the water surface.
Reason (R): Mosquito larvae and pupae live in water but need air to respire.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q:
Read the statements about mosquitoes.
I. The adult mosquito that comes out of the pupa rests briefly on the water surface and then flies away.
II. Mosquito larvae and pupae can stay under water all the time, because they do not need air.
III. The adult female mosquito lays her eggs only on dry ground, far away from water.
Which of these statements is or are correct?
questions.a: I only
o: I only
I and II only
I and III only
II and III only

questions.q: (a) Name the two worm-like stages of the mosquito that can be found in stagnant water. (b) Name two common places where stagnant water is likely to gather.
questions.a: (a) Larva and pupa. (b) Any two of: desert coolers, planted pots, open containers.
s: (a) Larva and pupa
(b) Any two of desert coolers, planted pots, open containers

questions.q: True or False? 'Spraying kerosene oil on stagnant water kills the adult mosquitoes flying above it.' Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: False. The kerosene forms a thin layer on the water surface that separates the water from the air, so the larvae and pupae in the water cannot get air and die. It acts on the larvae and pupae, not on the flying adults.
s: Verdict: False
Reason: the kerosene layer cuts off air from the larvae and pupae in the water, so they die

questions.q: Ravi fills Jar 1 with puddle water holding only mosquito larvae, and Jar 2 with the same puddle water holding only mosquito pupae. After four days, Jar 1 has some pupae but no adults. Jar 2 has winged mosquitoes resting on the water surface and no larvae at all. (a) What does Jar 1 show? (b) What does Jar 2 show? (c) Write the full life cycle in order, showing where the egg fits in.
questions.a: (a) Larvae change into pupae, so the larva stage comes before the pupa stage. (b) Adult mosquitoes come out of pupae, so the pupa stage comes just before the adult. (c) Egg, larva, pupa, adult; the adult female lays eggs on or near water and the cycle continues.
s: (a) Larvae turn into pupae: larva comes before pupa
(b) Adults come out of pupae: pupa comes just before adult
(c) Egg, larva, pupa, adult, with the female laying eggs on or near water

questions.q: Rekha checks her desert cooler. She finds many worm-like creatures swimming in the water but no flying mosquitoes. She says, 'There are no mosquitoes here, so I do not need to empty the cooler.' Check her claim.
questions.a: Her claim is wrong. The worm-like creatures are mosquito larvae and pupae, which are stages of the mosquito's life cycle. The larvae will grow into pupae and the pupae will turn into adult mosquitoes that fly away; the adult females lay eggs on or near water and the cycle continues. So the stagnant water in the cooler is letting mosquitoes breed, and she should empty it.
s: Says the claim is wrong: the worm-like creatures are mosquito larvae and pupae
Explains that they become adults, and females lay more eggs on or near water
Concludes the stagnant water lets mosquitoes breed, so the cooler should be emptied

questions.q: A teacher gives the class four cards about mosquitoes, in jumbled order. Card P: a winged insect that rests briefly on the water surface and then flies away. Card Q: laid by the adult female directly on or near water. Card R: a worm-like creature in the water that later changes into the creature on Card S. Card S: a worm-like creature of a different shape that also rises to the surface for air, and from which the winged insect comes out. (a) Name the stage on each card. (b) Arrange the cards in the order of the life cycle. (c) Which two cards show stages that a thin layer of kerosene on the water would kill, and why? (d) For about how long may the stage on Card P survive, and what does it do that keeps the cycle going?
questions.a: (a) P: adult; Q: egg; R: larva; S: pupa. (b) Q, R, S, P. (c) R and S: the larvae and pupae live in water but come to the surface for air; the kerosene layer separates the water from the air, so they cannot inhale air and die. (d) About 10 to 15 days; the adult female lays eggs on or near water, so the cycle continues.
s: (a) P adult, Q egg, R larva, S pupa
(b) Order Q, R, S, P
(c) R and S, because kerosene cuts off their air at the surface
(d) 10 to 15 days; the female lays eggs on or near water

questions.q:
Health workers check the campus of a primary health centre in a village near Nalgonda after the rains. They count mosquito larvae and pupae at three kinds of spots. Desert cooler in the waiting room (water not changed for 10 days): 28 larvae, 6 pupae. A rain-filled pit in the garden that cannot be emptied: 40 larvae, 9 pupae. Fifteen flower-pot trays: 2 larvae in each tray, no pupae.
(a) How many larvae were found in all?
(b) Into which stage will the pupae change next, and why does that make the problem urgent?
(c) The pit cannot be emptied. Which method from the chapter can stop the larvae and pupae in it, and how does it work?
(d) The caretaker has time for only one job today: empty and dry the cooler and all fifteen trays, or treat the pit. Which should he do first? Use the counts to justify your choice.
questions.a: (a) 28 + 40 + (15 x 2) = 98 larvae. (b) Into adult mosquitoes, which fly away, and the adult females lay eggs on or near water, so the cycle spreads. (c) Pour a thin layer of kerosene oil on the water: it separates the water from the air, so the larvae and pupae cannot inhale air and die. (d) Either choice is accepted with a reason from the data. Emptying the cooler and trays removes 28 + 6 + 30 = 64 larvae and pupae, more than the pit's 40 + 9 = 49, and leaves no water there. Treating the pit first deals with more pupae (9 against 6), which are closest to becoming adults.
s: (a) 98 larvae
(b) Adults; they fly off and females lay eggs on or near water
(c) A thin layer of kerosene cuts the larvae and pupae off from air
(d) A choice justified with the counts (64 against 49) or the pupae (9 against 6)

questions.q: After rain, two puddles form near a school. Puddle X is on open, sunny ground and dries up completely the next day. Puddle Y is in a shaded corner behind a shed and holds water for three weeks after every rain. Female mosquitoes lay eggs at both puddles. (a) In which puddle can mosquitoes reach the adult stage? (b) What happens to any larvae in Puddle X when it dries, and why? (c) Which stages in Puddle Y keep coming to the surface, and why? (d) Suggest one way, other than kerosene, to stop mosquitoes breeding in Puddle Y. (e) Explain why killing only the adult mosquitoes around the school will not stop the problem if Puddle Y is left as it is.
questions.a: (a) Puddle Y. (b) They die, because larvae (and pupae) live in water and cannot complete their growth once the water is gone. (c) The larvae and pupae; they live in water but need air to respire, so they come up to the surface for air. (d) Do not let water stagnate there: drain the puddle or fill the low spot with soil so that water cannot collect. (e) The larvae and pupae in Puddle Y keep turning into new adults, and the adult females lay eggs on or near water again, so the life cycle continues.
s: (a) Puddle Y
(b) Larvae in X die because they live in water and the water is gone
(c) Larvae and pupae come up for air to respire
(d) Drain or fill the puddle so water cannot stagnate
(e) Larvae and pupae keep becoming adults, and females lay more eggs on or near water

questions.q: On a pond visit, students see a white jelly-like mass at the edge of the water. What is this frog spawn?
questions.a: A cluster of frog eggs
o: A cluster of frog eggs
A group of young tadpoles
A cluster of froglets
A layer of pond plants

questions.q:
Match each stage of the frog's life cycle in Column I with the time at which it appears, as shown in the chapter, in Column II.
Column I: 1. Spawn 2. Embryo 3. Froglet 4. Adult frog

Which of these statements are correct?

questions.q: (a) What are young frogs that have started to look like little frogs called? (b) How does its tail help a tadpole?
questions.a: (a) Froglets. (b) The tail helps the tadpole swim in water.
s: (a) Froglets
(b) The tail helps it swim in water

questions.q: On a pond visit, Neeraj sees two young frogs. Animal P has a tail and no legs. Animal Q has a tail and two hind legs. (a) Which of the two is at an earlier stage? (b) Describe the next stage that Q will grow into.
questions.a: (a) P, the tadpole with a tail and no legs (the early tadpole stage). (b) Q will grow into a froglet: it starts to look like a little frog and still lives in water, but begins to spend some time on land.
s: (a) P is at the earlier stage
(b) Q becomes a froglet: looks like a little frog, lives in water but begins to spend time on land

questions.q: Divya says: 'A froglet is just a smaller copy of an adult frog. It looks like a frog and lives the same way.' Is she right, wrong, or partly right? Explain.
questions.a: Partly right. A froglet does look like a little frog. But it does not live the same way: a froglet still lives in water and only begins to spend some time on land, while an adult frog lives both in water and on land. The froglet still has to grow, lose its tail completely and develop strong legs for jumping before it becomes an adult.
s: Verdict: partly right; a froglet does look like a little frog
Habitat differs: froglet lives in water and only begins to go on land; adult lives in water and on land
The froglet must still lose its tail completely and get strong legs for jumping

questions.q: Ira says, 'A mosquito larva is just the mosquito's tadpole.' (a) Give two ways in which a mosquito larva and a tadpole are alike. (b) Give one way in which the comparison is wrong.
questions.a: (a) Both are the stage that comes after the egg, and both live in water. (b) A mosquito larva changes into a pupa before the adult comes out, while a tadpole grows legs and becomes a froglet and then an adult frog; there is no pupa in the frog's life cycle.
s: (a) First likeness: both come after the egg stage
(a) Second likeness: both live in water
(b) The larva becomes a pupa before the adult, while the tadpole becomes a froglet (no pupa in a frog)

questions.q: The changes in a frog's body during its life cycle help it survive where it lives at each stage. Explain how each change suits the animal: (a) an early tadpole has a tail and no legs; (b) a later tadpole has grown hind legs but still keeps its tail; (c) a froglet begins to spend some time on land; (d) the adult frog has lost its tail completely and has strong legs.
questions.a: (a) The early tadpole lives in water, and its tail helps it swim. (b) It still lives in water, so it still needs its tail to swim, while its legs are developing for the stages to come. (c) It now looks like a little frog with growing legs, so it can start to move onto land, though it still lives mostly in water. (d) The adult lives both in water and on land; strong legs help it jump and land, so it no longer needs a tail for swimming.
s: (a) Tail helps the early tadpole swim in water
(b) Still lives in water, so it keeps the tail while legs develop
(c) Frog-like body and growing legs let it begin moving onto land
(d) Adult lives in water and on land; strong legs for jumping replace the tail

questions.q:
An eco-club in Bhopal kept a record of the young frogs in its school pond after frog spawn was seen. Spawn seen: Day 1. Embryo: Day 3. Tadpole with a tail and no legs: Day 8. Tadpole with hind legs: Day 63. Froglet: Day 84. Adult frog: Day 98. Each stage lasts until the next one appears.
(a) For how many days was the young frog a tadpole with a tail and no legs?
(b) For how many days did the froglet stage last?
(c) Which stage lasted the shortest time? Show the working.
(d) The club can visit only once more and wants to see a stage that has started to spend some time on land. Should it visit on Day 70 or on Day 90? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 63 - 8 = 55 days. (b) 98 - 84 = 14 days. (c) The spawn stage: 3 - 1 = 2 days (embryo 5 days, tadpole with tail 55 days, tadpole with hind legs 21 days, froglet 14 days). (d) Day 90. On Day 90 the young frogs are froglets (Day 84 to Day 98), which still live in water but begin to spend some time on land. On Day 70 they are tadpoles with hind legs, which still live in water.
s: (a) 55 days
(b) 14 days
(c) Spawn stage, 2 days, compared with the other stages
(d) Day 90: the froglet stage begins to spend time on land; on Day 70 they are tadpoles living in water

questions.q: A classroom poster says: 'Every living being has the same life cycle: it starts small, grows bigger, and dies. Nothing else happens.' Evaluate the poster using the life cycles of the bean plant, the mosquito and the frog. (a) State one part of the poster that is true for all three. (b) How does the life cycle of a bean plant begin and continue, unlike that of the two animals? (c) Name a stage in the mosquito's life cycle that the frog's life cycle does not have. (d) Name one change in the frog's life cycle that the poster leaves out completely. (e) Give your overall verdict on the poster, with one reason.
questions.a: (a) All three grow through several stages and finally die. (b) The bean plant begins as a seed and grows into a plant that makes flowers and fruits (pods) with seeds; the seeds start the next generation. The mosquito and the frog begin as eggs. (c) The pupa (or the larva). (d) A change of habitat: the frog moves from living in water (as a tadpole) to living both in water and on land (as an adult); or the big change in body shape, such as losing the tail. (e) The poster is partly right but incomplete: it leaves out reproduction, through which each living being produces new ones of its own kind so the cycle continues, and the large changes in body shape and habitat seen in mosquitoes and frogs.
s: (a) All three grow through stages and die
(b) The bean plant starts as a seed and its seeds start the next generation; the animals start as eggs
(c) Names the pupa or the larva
(d) Names the change of habitat (water to water and land) or the change in body shape
(e) Partly right: it misses reproduction and continuity of the cycle, and changes in body shape and habitat
